meta.title: Religion, Family & Marriage Dataset — 5 Countries
meta.description: Comprehensive cultural dataset covering religious composition, family structure, marriage, funeral customs, superstition, LGBTQ rights, and secularization trends for Indonesia, Australia, Italy, Singapore, and Malaysia.
sources: US State Department International Religious Freedom Reports

dataPoints.value: Widespread especially in Chinese-majority business sector; SMEs consult geomancers for office layout, grand opening dates, floor numbers, phone/company registration numbers

dataPoints.value: Filial piety legally mandated via Maintenance of Parents Act 1995; elderly can sue children for maintenance. Institutional care (nursing homes) growing but stigmatized.
dataPoints.source: Singapore Statutes Online — Maintenance of Parents Act

dataPoints.metric: Islam as state religion — business implications
dataPoints.value: Sharia law applies to Muslims in personal/family matters. Halal certification required for Muslim consumers. Friday prayers: government offices and many businesses in Johor, Kedah, Kelantan, Terengganu close Friday afternoons.
dataPoints.source: US State Department Religious Freedom Report Malaysia 2023

dataPoints.notes: One of world's highest public holiday counts when state holidays added (up to 18-20 days). Hari Raya Puasa (2d), Hari Raya Haji, Maulidur Rasul, CNY (2d), Wesak, Deepavali, Thaipusam (some states), National Day, Malaysia Day, Labour Day, Agong's Birthday, Ruler's birthday (per state)

dataPoints.source: Destination Asia / Wikipedia Public Holidays Malaysia

dataPoints.notes: Down 8.7% from 63,338 in 2022

dataPoints.value: Non-Muslim must convert to Islam to marry a Muslim. Civil Marriage Act 1976 explicitly excludes Muslims. Marriages overseas not recognized if couple returns to Malaysia.

dataPoints.metric: Apostasy law — Muslim leaving Islam to marry non-Muslim
dataPoints.value: Requires Sharia court approval (rarely granted). Some states (Kelantan, Terengganu) have death penalty for apostasy on books (never applied). Practical barrier is near-absolute.
dataPoints.source: Wikipedia Freedom of Religion Malaysia / US State Department 2023

dataPoints.notes: Bumiputera/Malay TFR ~2.4; Chinese ~1.4; Indian ~1.8 (ethnic variation)

dataPoints.value: Common especially in Malay and Indian communities; Chinese community shows higher rate of nuclear households in urban areas
dataPoints.source: Manulife Diverse Asia Family Structural Change report

dataPoints.value: Filial piety strong across all ethnic groups; formal care homes under-resourced and socially stigmatized; family care primary especially for Malay-Muslim households
dataPoints.source: Manulife Diverse Asia report / DOSM elderly care data

dataPoints.value: Criminalized: Section 377A Penal Code (up to 20 years + whipping for anal/oral sex). Sharia laws add additional state-level penalties for Muslims.

dataPoints.metric: Feng shui / Chinese superstition in business and real estate
dataPoints.value: Significant economic influence; cemetery-facing properties sell at discount; lucky numbers (8, 6) command premium in car plate auctions, phone numbers, property addresses; kai gong (auspicious business opening) widely practiced
dataPoints.source: Planning Malaysia Journal / empirical studies on car plate auctions

dataPoints.value: Avoiding certain days for contracts; reciting bismillah before business opening; belief in rezeki (divinely apportioned income); not whistling inside buildings; superstitions around keris and traditional weapons
dataPoints.source: Cultural Atlas Malaysia / academic studies on Malay cultural beliefs

dataPoints.value: Prohibited under Sharia (zina); khalwat (close proximity) enforcement active; non-Muslim cohabitation socially tolerated but not legally recognized
dataPoints.source: US State Department Religious Freedom Report Malaysia 2023

dataPoints.value: Inter-ethnic dating common but marriage faces legal barriers (Muslim conversion requirement). Chinese-Indian coupling more common than Malay-Chinese/Indian. Social pressure from family significant across all communities.
dataPoints.source: Quora community surveys / academic interfaith marriage studies Malaysia

dataPoints.value: Faraid (Islamic inheritance) — compulsory for Muslims; courts apply Sharia-prescribed shares. Non-Muslims follow civil Probate and Administration Act 1959.
dataPoints.source: Malaysian Sharia courts / legal practice guides

dataPoints.notes: Only Indonesia above replacement rate (2.1); Singapore dangerously below at 0.97

dataPoints.metric: Superstition influence on business decisions — relative scale

value.Singapore: High — feng shui, numerology, auspicious dates mainstream in Chinese business
value.Malaysia: High — Chinese community feng shui + Malay pantang larang
value.Indonesia: Moderate-High — Javanese weton calendar, slametan ceremonies, Balinese ritual calendar
value.Italy: Low-Moderate — malocchio, number 17, patron saint days affect local commerce

dataPoints.metric: Elder care model — family vs institutional

value.Indonesia: Family-primary; no state pension system; filial duty cultural norm
value.Australia: Institutional-primary; NDIS + aged care system; family supplementary
value.Italy: Mixed; informal family care dominant (3/4 of care) despite high aging; institutional growing
value.Singapore: Legal filial piety obligation (Maintenance of Parents Act); institutional available but stigmatized
value.Malaysia: Family-primary; institutional care underdeveloped; strong filial norm all ethnicities

dataPoints.metric: Cohabitation before marriage — social acceptance level

value.Italy: Growing; ~50% of under-35s; civil union rights for cohabitants
value.Singapore: Moderate; growing among Chinese; conservative in Malay-Muslim community
value.Malaysia: Low-Very Low; illegal for Muslims (zina/khalwat); tolerated for non-Muslims
value.Indonesia: Very Low; criminalized under 2022 Penal Code; strong social taboo

dataPoints.metric: Family involvement in career and marriage decisions — relative scale

value.Indonesia: Very High — family council expected for major decisions; parental approval mandatory in many cultures
value.Italy: High — especially in South; parents involved in career, housing, marriage choices; mammoni culture
value.Singapore: High — Confucian/Asian values; academic and career decisions heavily family-influenced
value.Malaysia: Very High — across all ethnicities; community and extended family input expected
